name: Equality contract silently broken by equals method typo (not overriding Object.equals)
description: A class intends to override Object.equals(Object) but contains a typo in the method name or signature (for example, equal(Object), equals(Complex), equals(Object, ...), wrong visibility/return type). As a result, the method does not override Object.equals, and Java collections and frameworks continue to use reference equality. This causes subtle protocol/state bugs: deduplication fails, cache keys miss, set membership breaks, and invariants relying on logical equality collapse even though the class appears to implement an equality method.

trigger_conditions.test_shape: Tests that rely on value-based equality, such as inserting logically identical objects into HashSet/HashMap and expecting deduplication or successful retrieval.
trigger_conditions.input_properties: Two distinct instances carry identical field values; code expects them to compare equal or map to the same set entry.

example.description: A protocol/session layer uses a value-like key (endpoint + sessionId + nonce) to deduplicate handshakes and cache per-session metadata in HashMap/HashSet. A refactor introduces an equality typo: the class defines equals(SessionKey) (or equal(Object)) instead of overriding equals(Object). Java collections therefore keep using reference equality, so logically identical keys created on subsequent parses do not match, leading to cache misses, duplicate sessions, and invariant failures without exceptions.
